                                    PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                       § PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                    §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                 §            OF TEXAS


     ADDITIONAL COMMENTS OF MONARCH ENERGY DEVELOPMENT LLC
          ON PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION OF NEW 16 TAC §25.194

       COMES NOW Monarch Energy Development LLC (Monarch) and files these additional

comments regarding the Proposal for Publication (PFP) of new 16 Texas Administrative Code

(TAC) §25.194 relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards, which would set forth the

standards and criteria for an electric utility to interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT

transmission network.

       At its March 12, 2026, Open Meeting, the Commission approved the PFP for publication

and comment, adopting key changes that improved the original Commission Staff draft proposal.

Monarch appreciates the changes the Commission made to reduce the amount of financial security

and the interconnection fee that must be posted, as well as providing additional flexibility for

demonstrating site control. As the deliberations of the Commission reflected, though, there

remained concerns about whether posting of financial security should be tiered to reflect

commercial development processes and the extent to which the financial security that is posted

should be refundable. Monarch agrees that these are critical issues that need attention quickly,

especially since ERCOT has proposed to apply the requirements of the PFP to Large Load

Customers that seek to participate in Batch Zero of the Large Load Batch Study Process in its

proposed Planning Guide Revision Request (PGRR) 145, Batch Zero Process for Large Load

Interconnections. This creates the risk of imminent harm to the ERCOT market.
        As proposed, draft 16 TAC §25.194 requires the developer of a 500 MW large load to post

$25,000,000 to find out from ERCOT if there is sufficient capacity to serve its proposed large load

on a commercially reasonable timeline. If there is insufficient capacity and the developer

withdraws its project from further consideration, the developer is penalized at least $20,000,000

as a non-refundable fee. Such a penalty bears no relation to cost causation – it is a penalty. Monarch

agrees that it would be more reasonable to implement the approach Google and Lancium

recommended in their March 10, 2026, proposed redlines 1 whereby a maximum of $6.5 million of

the financial security would be non-refundable following a preliminary steady state study.

       In addition, another concern that remains unresolved is the application of this new process

to Monarch and other developers who have been diligently working with TSPs and ERCOT to

interconnect large load projects for several years, even before the filing and effective date of SB

6. The process ERCOT has proposed in PGRR 145 will impose retroactive requirements that will

essentially reject all progress and investments that have been made on projects, such as where there

already is a signed Letter of Agreement (LOA) for financial security, and the Contribution in Aid

to Construction (CIAC) has been paid. While Monarch respectfully continues to object being

subject to the Batch Study process at all, Monarch agrees with the Google/Lancium Redlines 2

proposal to add the following clarification to the applicability of these new requirements:

       Any projects that have executed a signed agreement with the TSP prior to the
       effective date of this rule and have satisfied all CIAC and security payment
       obligations in accordance with the timelines specified in that agreement by the
       effective date of this rule shall be exempt from additional costs or security required
       by the following standards.




1
    Google LLC and Lancium LLC, Joint Redlines for the Proposal for Publication at 2-3 (March 10, 2026)
    (Google/Lancium Redlines).
2
    Id. at 5.

                                                        Monarch Energy Additional Comments - Page 2
 This clarification would mitigate the harm imposed by the Batch Study process to projects that

have been in development for years. In addition, projects that have met these requirements prior

to the effective date of PGRR 145 should also be included in Batch Zero as firm load so that they

can timely complete the development activities that they started years ago.

        Finally, ERCOT’s application of proposed rules that the Commission already has revised

should be revisited immediately. For example, in its Compliance Plan filed in Project No. 58480,

Rulemaking to Establish Large Load Forecasting Criteria Under PURA §37.0561, ERCOT

imposed a more restrictive approach to demonstrating site control for the proposed load location

than the Commission included in the PFP in this proceeding. 3 Given ERCOT’s representation in

its Compliance Plan that it does not need final load submissions from each Transmission and/or

Distribution Service Provider before April 1, 2026, ERCOT should implement this change in its

Compliance Plan immediately.

        Monarch appreciates the opportunity to submit these additional comments and looks

forward to working with the Commission and ERCOT to develop a workable batch study process

that supports continued growth in the ERCOT Region.

                                                                                   Respectfully submitted,


                                                                    ______/s/ Kevin Boudreaux______
                                                                                    Kevin Boudreaux
                                                                               Head of Power Supply
                                                                    Monarch Energy Development LLC
                                                                                      (832) 875-0969
                                                                       KBoudreaux@monarch.energy

                                                                                            March 19, 2026



3
    Rulemaking to Establish Large Load Forecasting Criteria Under PURA §37.0561, Project No. 58480, ERCOT’s
    Proposed Compliance Plan for Including Large Loads in the Load Forecast for the 2026 Regional Transmission
    Plan, Attachment A at p. 2 (January 22, 2026) (ERCOT Compliance Plan).

                                                           Monarch Energy Additional Comments - Page 3
